summary.headline: Running is on plan through week 3 (127.4 of 130.4 km, all 12 runs done), but strength and cycling are patchy and 1:30 still looks like a stretch.
observations: Weeks 1-3 gave 42.0, 42.0 and 43.4 km against 42.0, 45.0 and 43.4 planned. That is 98% of planned distance. Some earlier run reviews say you are far behind or that fitness is decaying, but the weekly totals and load data do not support that.

Long runs followed the plan exactly: 16.0, 17.0 and 18.6 km at 5:47, 5:50 and 5:52/km. HR drifted up from 142 to 143 to 146 bpm and efficiency fell from 1.218 to 1.200 to 1.169, so watch accumulating fatigue as the long run grows.
Easy runs are consistent at 5:42-5:50/km with HR 137-140, inside the 5:11-6:13 band and conversational. The long runs have 113-186 m of climb, while the easy runs are flat.

Tempo work is good when you are fresh. On 3 Nov and 17 Nov you hit 4:37 and 4:36/km for 4 km and 5 km at HR 161-163. On 10 Nov, after poor sleep and with heavy legs, the tempo fell to 5:00/km at HR 176 (RPE 8) and you stopped at 6 of 9 km. The next tempo showed no lingering effect.
The 19 Nov reps (4 × 0.4 km) averaged 4:00/km against 3:55 at HR 171, with a max of 174 bpm. That is about 5 s/km slow but controlled. The jogs ran at 6:20/km, slightly slower than the easy band.
Fitness is edging up: CTL went from 43.0 to a peak of 49.8 on 22 Nov, and is now 46.4 after three days off. TSB is -2.6, so you are not carrying much fatigue into the lighter week 4.

Strength and cross-training are the weak spot. Strength was 0 of 2 in weeks 1 and 2 and 2 of 2 in week 3. Cycling was done once in three weeks, in week 2. This matters for the achilles history, since calf and eccentric work is in the strength sessions.
Week 4 has nothing logged yet. The Tuesday 9 km easy run and Strength A from 24 Nov are missing, and today's 30 min ride is not logged yet.

On the goal: your 44:00 10 km is 4:24/km, and the half needs 4:16/km for twice the distance. Your tempo pace (4:36) has not changed since week 1, and no race-pace running appears until week 8 (6 km at 4:16). That equates to roughly a 1:35-1:36 half today.
suggestions: Do not make up Tuesday's missed 9 km. Pick up with Thursday's 4 × 0.4 km and keep the week-4 long run at 14.6 km as a true recovery week. If Tuesday was skipped for tiredness or a niggle, add a note.
Protect the strength sessions, especially the calf and eccentric work, and fit in the weekly ride. These are your injury insurance as mileage rises towards 52 km.
Log RPE and a short note on every run. Only one of 15 sessions has an RPE, which makes it hard to separate fatigue from a bad day.
Keep long-run pace relaxed, around 5:55-6:10/km, and keep HR near 140-145. Next time check whether the 146 bpm average at 18.6 km is a one-off or a trend.
Week 7 jumps to 52 km, about 20% above your biggest week so far (43.4 km). Consider capping it near 48-50 km if the achilles feels tight or the long-run HR keeps climbing.

Around weeks 6-7, run a 5 km or 10 km time trial, or a longer tempo, to check whether 1:30 is still realistic. Pick a fallback target such as 1:33-1:35 so race pace has a clear purpose, and consider adding some marathon-pace work before week 8.
